Chapter.Section: Philosophy FinInG (pronunciation: [\textipa{f\;I{}n\;I{}N}fɪnɪŋ]) is a package for computation in Finite Incidence Geometry. It provides users with the basic tools to work in various areas of finite geometry from the realms of projective spaces to the flat lands of generalised polygons. The algebraic power of GAP is employed, particularly in its facility with matrix and permutation groups. A sample making FinInG's pronunciation crystal clear can be found here.

How to cite FinInG The development group of FinInG welcomes contact with users. We are very interested in results obtained using FinInG, so please tell us about the use of FinInG in your research or teaching by sending an e-mail to council@fining.org. We might refer to your work in the future. If your work is published, we ask you to cite FinInG like a journal article or book.
If you are using BibTeX, you can use the following BibTeX entry for the current FinInG version:

Overview of this manual
This chapter (section ) describes the installation of the package. Chapter contains some extended examples to introduce the user to the basic functionality and philosophy to get started. Chapter contains a rigorous description of the basic structures. This chapter can be omitted at first reading, since the set of consequent chapters is also self contained. Chapters , and deal with projective spaces, projective semilinear groups and polarities of projective spaces, respectively. In Chapter the functionality for classical polar spaces is treated and in Chapter affine spaces and their groups are considered. Geometry morphisms between various geometries that are available in the package, are introduced and discussed in Chapter . The final three chapters, , , and explain the basic functionality which is provided for algebraic varieties (in projective or affine spaces), generalised polygons, of which several models can be constructed, and finally coset geometries and diagrams.

Getting and installing FinInG FinInG
FinInG is part of the &GAP; distribution, so it is already present in a standard &GAP; installation. It requires the packages cvec, Forms, GenSS, GRAPE and Orb, and cvec in turn requires IO. All of these are part of the &GAP; distribution too. The required versions are listed in the file PackageInfo.g of FinInG.
Compiling the required packages
Some of the required packages contain code that must be compiled:
IO and cvec must be compiled, otherwise FinInG cannot be loaded.
GRAPE uses the program nauty to compute automorphism groups of graphs. FinInG relies on this for the collineation groups of generalised polygons (see Chapter ) and for AutGroupIncidenceStructureWithNauty and IsIsomorphicIncidenceStructureWithNauty.
Orb works without compilation, but its compiled part makes it faster.
The &GAP; installer for Windows contains compiled versions of these packages, so no further steps are needed there. On Linux, macOS and other UNIX-like systems, use the script BuildPackages.sh that comes with &GAP;. Run it from the pkg directory of your &GAP; installation; when given package directories as arguments, it compiles only those:
cd /path/to/gap/pkg ../bin/BuildPackages.sh io* cvec* orb* grape*
Afterwards, start &GAP; and load FinInG. The output should end as follows.
gap> LoadPackage("fining"); ... --------------------------------------------------------------------- ______________ ________ _________ ___ ____/__(_)__________ _/________ ____/ __ /_ __ /__ __ __ / __ __ / __ _ __/ _ / _ / / /_/ / _ / / / /_/ / /_/ /_/ /_/ /_//___/ /_/ /_/____/ --------------------------------------------------------------------- Loading FinInG &VERSION; (Finite Incidence Geometry) by John Bamberg (https://johnbamberg.github.io) Anton Betten (https://www.math.colostate.edu/~betten) Philippe Cara (https://wids.research.vub.be/nl/philippe-cara) Jan De Beule (https://wids.research.vub.be/en/node/149) Michel Lavrauw (https://mlavrauw.github.io) Max Neunhoeffer For help, type: ?FinInG --------------------------------------------------------------------- true
If LoadPackage returns fail instead, enter SetInfoLevel(InfoPackageLoading, 4); and load the package again to see which requirement is missing.
Updating FinInG
New releases of FinInG are included in new releases of &GAP;, and are also available from https://github.com/gap-packages/FinInG/releases. To use a newer release with an existing &GAP; installation, unpack its archive in the pkg subdirectory of your user &GAP; root directory, which is given by GAPInfo.UserGapRoot (see ). If several versions of a package are installed, &GAP; loads the newest one that can be loaded. The PackageManager package can download and install releases into this directory for you.
